snippet.title: Speed Ball Longplay (Arcade Game)
snippet.description:
- Speed Ball Longplay (Arcade Game) -

Speed Ball, released by Tecfri in 1987, is a video pinball game that blends fast action with a three-table progression system reminiscent of Jaleco’s Pinball Action. Instead of a single board, the game shifts between themed playfields as the ball moves upward, giving each section a distinct look and feel. The first area takes inspiration from spy motifs with a clear nod to “007”; the second adopts a sci-fi atmosphere filled with spacecraft and glowing targets; and the third shifts into an ancient-Egypt theme dominated by a sphinx and stylised iconography.

The gameplay follows classic early video-pinball conventions: you control flippers placed at the bottom of each section and attempt to accumulate points by striking bumpers, activating targets and sending the ball up into the next screen. Like many Tecfri titles, Speed Ball moves quickly, with a lively rebound physics model that keeps the ball in constant danger of slipping through the central drain. Its difficulty is one of its defining traits; the ball escapes with little warning, and maintaining a rally long enough to cycle through the boards demands sharp reactions and a degree of luck.

Each screen introduces its own scoring quirks and bonus triggers. Extra balls, illuminated side lanes, brief mini-objectives and light-up point multipliers appear depending on the table, giving each theme a slightly different rhythm. The visuals are colourful and busy, and despite the limitations of the period, the game conveys personality through its themed backdrops and animated inserts. Sound effects remain simple but effective, built around short chimes and quick mechanical cues that reinforce the arcade-pinball blend.

Speed Ball is not widely remembered today, but it stands as a curious example of late-80s Spanish arcade development and an offbeat entry in the video-pinball niche. Its brisk pace, varied screens and high challenge level give it a rough charm, even if it can feel unforgiving. For players who enjoy difficult, old-school digital pinball, it remains an interesting and rarely discussed title.
